Hi Tessa,

I was going through the Quickstart in your docs earlier today and clicked the "Schedule technical demo" CTA — wanted to follow up directly. We are BuildByte (vector search + analytics for e‑commerce), and I'm the engineering lead on a project to replace our current inference pipeline. We're especially interested in latency at 99th percentile, batching behavior, and options for private deployment.

Would love a 30–45 min technical walkthrough focused on:
- serving architecture (KV cache, batching)
- quantization/throughput tradeoffs on T4/A10G
- integration with our vector DB + expected token costs

I'm in Pacific (PDT). I have openings: Wed 6/16 10:00–11:30, Thu 6/17 14:00–16:00, or Fri 6/18 09:00–11:00.

Attached a very small diagram of our current topology — "buildbyte-arch.png" — to give context.

Thanks,
Alex Rivera
Engineering Lead, BuildByte
alex.rivera@buildbyte.com
(415) 555-0182

Alex / Tessa — hi, I'm Soojin (Solutions Eng). Quick note on what I plan to cover and a couple of quick prep questions so we can make the call tactical: 

Planned coverage (30–45m):
- brief run-through of Redwood serving model (KV cache, continuous batching, fallback variants)
- latency/throughput tradeoffs and quantization options for T4/A10G
- recommended integration pattern for a vector DB + token cost ballpark for a sample workload

Quick prep Qs (one-liners are fine):
1) Expected sustained QPS for inference (or typical requests per minute)?
2) Typical input sequence length (avg / max tokens)?
3) Will inference see customer data you want persisted (yes/no) or do you plan ephemeral requests only?

Attaching a short integration checklist we use: "redwood-integration-checklist.pdf" — if you can drop answers inline and confirm a slot, we'll tailor the demo.

Thanks, looking forward to it.
Sooj

Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Thanks Tessa / Soojin — appreciate the quick replies.

Slot preference: Thu 6/17 — 14:30–15:15 (your 45m slot) looks best for our team, but would you be able to start 1 hour earlier (13:30–14:15) instead? We have a vendor sync that slipped into the late afternoon. If that doesn't work for your team, we can keep 14:30.

Quick answers to Soojin's questions:
1) Sustained QPS target initially ~8–12 qps, spike load up to ~40 qps during peak events.
2) Avg seq length ~120 tokens, max ~1,200 tokens (chat history + product context).
3) We will persist embeddings in our vector DB; raw request payloads are not stored beyond logging — so persistent context is at embeddings layer.

Attachment: attaching the diagram you have (buildbyte-arch.png) again in case it didn't come through.

If you confirm 13:30 PDT we will lock it on our side.

— Alex
